title: Fix: the shell that knows no commands
hints: The function works when the test passes a string literal like `"stop"` and fails when the same text sits in a `char` array. What is different about those two, as far as a pointer is concerned?

`c->name == name` compares two **addresses**, not the characters they point at. Two identical literals in one file usually share one address, so the literal case happens to work; a buffer filled at runtime lives somewhere else.
